intents.text: edit code over ssh: syntax highlighting, multiple buffers, no X11 and no clipboard integration
build small C projects locally with make
reach the machine over ssh with key auth only, no password auth, no X forwarding

never block the terminal on a long build: a terminal multiplexer that starts split into two panes, so a compile can run in one while I keep working in the other. Scriptable session and pane control from the shell. No mouse, no clipboard, no X.
serve this machine's ebuild tree and binary packages to other AIos nodes over HTTP, and take code updates from a peer the same way
rebuild the same package repeatedly without recompiling what did not change: a compiler cache sized for a few full package builds, shared across every build on this machine

make_conf.why: intent[4]: binary packages are shipped over the network to peers; fast compression keeps transfers small
intent[5]: one fixed cache location shared by all builds rather than per-user caches
intent[5]: sized to hold a few full package builds
intent[4]: stable path for the binary package directory that nginx exports over HTTP

intent[0]/intent[3]: no X11, no clipboard, no graphical session; intent[2]: no PAM since password auth is off; ssl kept globally because intent[2] key auth and intent[4] fetching need a crypto backend

notes: intent[1] (build small C projects with make): sys-devel/make, binutils and the compiler come from @system and the profile's toolchain, so no package is listed. Nothing extra is required.
intent[1], intent[2] and intent[4] have no probes, so the packages bound to them (openssh, nginx, git) can never be minimized away automatically.

No X-forwarding USE flag exists for net-misc/openssh; disabling X11Forwarding in sshd_config is a config-file decision for the renderer, not a build flag. Same for 'PasswordAuthentication no' / 'PubkeyAuthentication yes'.

tmux has no mouse or clipboard USE flag; 'no mouse, no clipboard' from intent[3] is enforced in tmux.conf (set -g mouse off, no set-clipboard), not at build time. The two-pane startup layout is likewise a tmux.conf/session-script concern.

intent[4] 'serve the ebuild tree over HTTP': nginx serving /var/db/repos/gentoo and PKGDIR as static directories covers this; if rsync export were wanted instead, net-misc/rsync would be needed — not added since HTTP was specified.

musl target: none of the listed packages are known to be glibc-only. app-editors/vim, app-misc/tmux, net-misc/openssh, dev-util/ccache, www-servers/nginx and dev-vcs/git all build on musl. nginx with certain third-party modules can need glibc-specifics; only the core static/autoindex modules are enabled here.
Assumed the peer code updates in intent[4] arrive as a git repository over HTTP. If they arrive as a plain rsync/HTTP snapshot instead, dev-vcs/git is unnecessary and should be dropped.
discarded agent-proposed FEATURES='ccache buildpkg parallel-fetch': spec-owned (kept 'buildpkg parallel-fetch -sandbox -usersandbox -userpriv -ipc-sandbox -network-sandbox -pid-sandbox')
